LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Commander.label: Commander
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Commander.description: A heavy command mech designed specifically for unmanned battlefields. Equipped with a high-output communications array and a precision tactical coordination system, it can offload bandwidth and coordinate commands for large numbers of mech units in real time while accurately relaying a mechanitor's control signals.\n\nWhat sets the Commander apart is that it is more than a simple relay node. Its onboard tactical processor grants it an independent bandwidth pool and the ability to control mechanoids on its own, and the units under its command are not limited by normal command range. As a result, many fleets deploy Commanders to frontier outposts and long-range expeditionary missions as frontline command cores capable of leading entire mech detachments independently.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Shaman.label: Shaman
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Shaman.description: An experimental mech equipped with a psychic device. The psychic system built into its frame can stimulate a psychic field in a specific manner, causing itself and nearby allies to "disappear" on the perceptual level, thereby achieving psychic concealment and disrupting detection.\n\nBecause of its exorbitant production cost, only a handful of Shamans ever appear on the front line. Most are reserved for high-risk infiltration, decapitation, and elimination missions—and such missions usually mean that the situation is no longer under normal control... or perhaps simply that this particular operation is considered important enough to warrant it.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Scout.label: Scout
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Scout.description: A high-mobility mech equipped with advanced biomimetic technology and movement computation systems. Its dynamic mobility module continuously gathers terrain and motion data while moving and adjusts its path in real time, pushing the output potential of its artificial muscle fibers to the limit. As long as it keeps moving, the Scout gradually builds up speed, and after covering enough ground it can even ignore the effects of difficult terrain on its movement.\n\n"When people speak of a cavalry charge, they usually think of heavily armored knights from the Middle Ages. And yet the same scene now plays out on the battlefield once more—absurd, but no less devastating." — From the combat record of a mechanitor.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Guardian.label: Guardian
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Guardian.description: A heavy assault mech designed for high-intensity combat. Its chassis uses multilayer composite armor and a reinforced structural frame, allowing it to keep advancing under frontal fire pressure while routinely undertaking assaults, defensive operations, and suppressive actions against fortified positions. Its integrated combat system can accommodate weapons of different classes, including certain heavy armaments, allowing it to adapt to complex and ever-changing battlefield conditions.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Arsonist.label: Arsonist
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Arsonist.description: A special-purpose mech designed for high-temperature environments. Its frame is fitted with a specialized heat-resistant structure and a flame projector, allowing it to continuously purge targets in confined spaces and underground facilities. It also mounts an additional close-range flame module on its arm, giving it a chance to ignite targets during melee combat.\n\nTo avoid friendly fire and structural blazes, deployments of the Arsonist usually require additional authorization. In most situations where one is needed, however, the approval process is often slower than the spread of the fire.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_SupportFrame.label: Support Frame
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_SupportFrame.description: One of the improved derivative models of the Battle Friend, created to test the practical viability of heavy weapons on walking platforms. Its frame has been specially reinforced for load-bearing capacity and recoil control, allowing it to stably operate heavy armaments that ordinary walkers would struggle to handle. As a result, it is often used as an accompanying fire support unit during infantry advances.
LanguageData.DMSL_Drone_CommandingBird.label: Commanding Bird
LanguageData.DMSL_Drone_CommandingBird.description: A mini command drone deployed from the belt to help the mechanitor direct combat from behind the lines.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Terra.label: Terra
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Terra.description: A special-purpose mech once used for assault and airborne operations. Its frame features a special biomimetic structure that allows it to freely wear most human equipment, giving it considerable flexibility in both mission execution and equipment use. Even now, in an era when synthroid technology has already matured, Terra still retains a place in legion formations thanks to its relatively low production cost and acceptable combat performance.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Engineer.label: Engineer
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Engineer.description: A mass-produced engineering mech. Its multifunctional work arms are capable not only of repairing mechs, but also of performing manufacturing and facility construction tasks with equally impressive efficiency. Its advanced maintenance system allows it to repair most conventional damage and, when conditions permit, even restart mechanoids that have already shut down.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Commandos.label: Commandos
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_Commandos.description: A general-purpose mech designed for mobile units. Its integrated combat system allows it to use nearly all human weapons, while its high mobility enables it to meet the demands of field operations.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_SpecialPolice.label: Special Police
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_SpecialPolice.description: A police mech used for riot suppression. Equipped with a high-voltage stun device, it can incapacitate targets in an instant; its built-in jumping apparatus also ensures rapid mobility so it can be committed to suppression actions in time.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_DesignatedMarksman.label: Designated Marksman
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_DesignatedMarksman.description: One of the improved derivative models of the Sniper. While preserving long-range shooting precision as much as possible, this model further reduces both assembly and bandwidth costs and improves the mech's overall performance. The price paid is that the Designated Marksman's skill level is lower than that of the original model.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_ArmoredGrenadiers.label: Armored Grenadiers
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_ArmoredGrenadiers.description: One of the improved derivative models of the Grenadier. This model further upgrades the original assembly process, trading a higher production cost for comprehensive improvements in protection, sustained firepower, and battlefield survivability. At the same time, its weapon compatibility has been expanded beyond that of the Grenadier: in addition to various grenade launchers and thrown explosives, it can also use more conventional weapons as the situation demands, allowing it to handle more complex high-intensity combat environments.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_DoctorFrame.label: Doctor Frame
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_DoctorFrame.description: An improved variant of the combat frame that can perform doctoring and cooking. You wouldn't use it for anything but saving lives, would you?
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_AgriculturalFrame.label: Agricultural Frame
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_AgriculturalFrame.description: An improved variant of the combat frame for farming tasks. Often a symbol of peace and love in literature. Drops 2-3 extra hay when harvesting.
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_DrillingBarge.label: Drilling Barge
LanguageData.DMSL_Mech_DrillingBarge.description: An improved variant of the combat frame, primarily for mining—it can also operate deep drills to extract underground deposits.
